item.title: Aichi Events 2026: Nagoya Sumo, Fireworks, Tenno Festival & Ghibli Park
item.description: Aichi — with Nagoya at its heart — is the manufacturing engine of Japan, but its 2026 event calendar is pure summer spectacle and samurai heritage. The prefecture hosts a July Grand Sumo tournament in a brand-new arena, some of the country’s biggest fireworks in its “Mikawa fireworks” heartland, a 600-year-old UNESCO river festival, a procession of the three warlords who unified Japan, and Studio Ghibli’s own theme park. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end.

item.title: Noritake Garden: Porcelain Craft in a Red-Brick Park — Guide
item.description: Noritake Garden occupies the site of the original 1904 works of Noritake, the porcelain maker whose fine tableware graced dinner tables worldwide, and turns the old factory grounds into a leafy urban park framed by red-brick workshops and the chimney stubs of former kilns. The craft centre is the heart of the visit: you watch artisans shape, fire and hand-paint porcelain at every stage, browse a museum of the company’s dazzling early ‘Old Noritake’ art pieces, and can even paint your own design onto a plate before browsing the outlet shop’s tableware bargains.

item.title: Tea Ceremony in Nagoya: The Oribe Tradition — Guide
item.description: Nagoya sits at the heart of the tea culture shaped by Furuta Oribe, the samurai tea master who succeeded Sen no Rikyu and stamped the ceremony with a bolder, more playful spirit — deliberately warped bowls, dramatic green-glazed Oribe ware from the region’s kilns, and an embrace of imperfection livelier than his teacher’s austerity. Tea-ceremony experiences in and around the city welcome beginners into tatami tea rooms to learn the gestures, whisk their own bowl of matcha and taste seasonal wagashi sweets, with some sessions held in historic gardens and machiya townhouses that deepen the sense of stepping into another century.

item.title: Best Hotels & Ryokan in Aichi: Nagoya, Inuyama & Beyond
item.description: Aichi Prefecture is anchored by Nagoya — Japan’s fourth-largest city and the industrial and cultural capital of the Chubu region. The prefecture also contains Inuyama (one of Japan’s 12 surviving original castles), the Chita Peninsula coastal onsen, and Meiji Mura open-air architecture museum. Best Areas to Stay Nagoya Station Area The main Shinkansen stop with direct connections to Tokyo (1h40min), Kyoto (35min), and Osaka (50min). Towers and hotels surround the station.
